Subject: Patent assertion notice / indemnity carveouts (Order Form)

Mina —

Thanks for taking this on. We reviewed the MSA + Order Form and have a few material concerns on the IP indemnity and defense-control mechanics that we need to resolve before legal can recommend signing. Attached are our suggested redlines (GCTech_redlines_20280810.docx). High-level: 

- Patent claims related to models trained on public or third-party data: we need an explicit carveout for claims that arise from Customer-provided data or from public-domain training sources.
- Defense control: our policy requires Customer control of defense where potential exposure exceeds $5M or where injunctive relief could materially impact operations. We can accept Redwood defense for smaller claims but want a right to assume control in specified circumstances.
- Cap on damages: we prefer a liability cap tied to fees for the 12-month period.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to: (a) add the carveout language for training data/published models; (b) propose a middle-ground on defense control that protects both sides; and (c) provide any flexibility on the cap for large enterprise deals?

We have a hard internal timeline — GC leadership expects counsel sign-off by end of next week. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Julia — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. I appreciate the timeline — we will prioritize. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (AE) so we can work a compromise that clears internal approvals quickly.

Quick responses to your three asks:
1) Training-data carveout: we understand the ask and will propose narrow language to exclude claims based solely on Customer-provided training data or public-domain sources. We need to confirm the exact drafting with Legal to avoid overbroad exclusions.
2) Defense control: Redwood’s standard is that we will defend and control defense for indemnifiable third-party IP claims, but we are open to a switch-control mechanism if Customer demonstrates material prejudice or if Redwood declines to defend within a defined window. We will circulate a couple of options.
3) Cap flexibility: for enterprise deals we can consider a higher tiered cap (or excess insurance layer) as part of the Order Form. Marissa — can you confirm commercial flexibility on committed spend?

Team / Julia —

Per Mina’s note, attached is a brief with three pragmatic approaches and a recommended redline (Redwood_response_markup_20280812.pdf). Options (high level):

Option A — Redwood sole defense control (Redwood defends and selects counsel). Customer retains right to participate at its own cost, and can assume control only if Redwood fails to prosecute/defend after 30 days. Limited carveouts for Customer data and OSS as described below. This minimizes coordination risk and preserves Redwood’s playbook.

Option B — Shared / trigger-based control (recommended). Redwood will defend initial proceedings. If potential exposure exceeds $5M or if injunctive relief is sought that could materially interfere with Customer operations, Customer may assume defense control (with Redwood’s consent not to be unreasonably withheld) after notice; if Redwood objects, escalation to senior counsel within 10 business days. Includes narrow carveout for claims arising solely from Customer-provided training data or known third-party contributions.

Option C — Customer-first control for high-risk claims. Customer controls defense for any patent-related claim; Redwood reimburses defense fees subject to reasonableness and a pre-set cap. This protects Customer but increases Redwood’s exposure/cost unpredictability.

My recommendation is Option B as a balanced operational compromise. Draft redline attached. Key open points we need from the Customer: example facts or scenarios where they expect to assert exclusion (helps tailor carveout), and confirmation on the $5M trigger (Customer proposed $5M threshold — please confirm).

Attaching latest Order Form iteration (OrderForm_v3_20280814.docx) which includes commercial terms and standard liability cap language; commercial will need to confirm whether a tiered cap is an option.

Kimberly / Mina —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for laying out options. Our in-house team reviewed Option B and we can live with a trigger-based approach provided that:

- The $5M threshold remains (we will not accept a lower trigger).
- If Customer assumes control, Redwood must reasonably cooperate and not appoint counsel that creates a conflict or prolongs litigation.
- Carveout language must specifically call out: (i) claims arising solely from Customer-supplied proprietary training data, and (ii) claims related to third-party open-source model weights and datasets where Customer can show provenance.

We are not comfortable with language that allows Redwood an open-ended 30-day window to decline defense without meaningful good-faith standards. Can we meet on Tuesday 15th at 11:00 PT to lock this? If you can share a redline of the exact paragraph we can mark final.
